speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Rota's finite-field Ramsey conjecture
summary: The dated lower block formulates a Ramsey assertion for subspaces over a fixed finite field, notes the known line case, and translates that case into projective language. The number of colors is suppressed in the notebook; it must be fixed before the ambient dimension is chosen. This is the vector-space Ramsey conjecture, not Rota\'s matroid-basis conjecture.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Thompson quadratic pairs and Conway's lattice group
summary: Gelfand reports Thompson\'s quadratic-pair classification. Kirillov then relays Thompson\'s account of Conway\'s sporadic group through a 24-dimensional lattice. The passage needs two distinctions: groups of Lie type are broader than classical groups, and the full automorphism group of the Leech lattice is a central double cover of the simple group. The reading list below this discussion is not a mathematical theorem.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A proposed non-quasi-coherent sheaf and a localization reminder
summary: This short intervention starts at the dated Gelfand heading and ends before Bernstein\'s example. Its proposed point-supported sheaf lacks enough module-structure data to justify the advertised counterexample.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Regular functions on affine varieties and the module/sheaf correspondence
summary: Bernstein\'s example is followed through its ideal-sheaf sequence, the supported-section gluing argument, and the presentation argument for quasi-coherent sheaves. The distinction between one global denominator and a locally regular function is made explicitly in the manuscript.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: States of a one-dimensional quantum spin chain
summary: The lecture constructs the quasi-local matrix algebra, states and their density matrices, diagonal classical states, finite-temperature Gibbs limits, and the GNS representation. The existence and factor questions are revisited in records 197 and 200.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Affine acyclicity by localization and Čech cochains
summary: The proof works with a finite distinguished-open cover. It includes both an explicit denominator-clearing attempt and Bernstein\'s annihilator argument; the manuscript itself acknowledges that localization equalities need more care.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Commuting densities, classical measures, and a failed diagonalization claim
summary: The quantum-state construction is repeated, now with partial traces. The assertion that mutually commuting embedded marginals admit a fixed sitewise product eigenbasis fails in the presence of degeneracies; an explicit faithful counterexample is supplied in the chapter\'s audit annotation.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Four subspaces: classification, normal forms, and deformation
summary: Gelfand reports joint work with V. A. Ponomarev. The graph examples and most displayed normal forms match the 1971 Doklady announcement very closely. The defect sign, missing odd-dimensional defect-zero systems, and broad stability assertions require separate audit; the classification itself is established.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: A repaired affine proof, a Picard-group exercise, and logarithmic forms
summary: The Kazhdan block begins after the four-subspace discussion on P000317. The brief Deligne theorem at the top of P000319 precedes Sinai\'s explicit heading and is recorded here as an unattributed mathematical report, not assigned a new speaker by guesswork.

speaker: Ya. G. Sinai
title: Powers' factor criterion and asymptotic independence
summary: The whole Sinai block is on P000319 below the separator. Its principal formula has an existential quantifier where a uniform tail-algebra estimate is needed; the original Powers theorem resolves that compression exactly.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Punctured affine space, Koszul exactness, and residue duality
summary: The manuscript\'s 16/XI date supplies the ISO date missing from the catalog\'s underscore-spelled entry. The computation is valid, but the final module-Hom identification is not: the residue pairing produces a restricted linear dual, not \(\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,k)\).

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Plans for the next semester
summary: The plan names Arnold and Gabrielov on Griffiths and integrals of rational differential forms over cycles; S. Gelfand on Brauer theory; Sinai on factors; Knorr on a new proof of a theorem of Grauert; and new work of Atiyah on skew Fredholm operators, alongside Gohberg, Krupnik, and Gorin. These are proposed subjects, with no precise new theorem asserted. The catalog dates this record 23 November, whereas the clearly visible manuscript header reads 22/XI. The isolated Arnold heading on P000325, about vector fields in general position, supplies no mathematical statement and is preserved here as an uncatalogued heading between Gorin and Kazhdan.

speaker: E. A. Gorin
title: Symbol algebras, the Arens–Royden index, and Toeplitz operators
summary: The Gorin block begins at the boxed name in the lower part of P000324 and ends before the isolated Arnold heading on P000325. It passes from a quotient by characters to a group-valued index, then gives the completed-curve Fredholm criterion for piecewise continuous Toeplitz symbols. These are reports on established Banach-algebra and Gohberg--Krupnik results; the manuscript does not identify a separate new Gorin theorem.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Projective space, Serre twists, and coherent cohomology
summary: Kazhdan constructs projective space and its twisting sheaves, states global generation, cohomological finiteness and vanishing, and proves polynomiality of Euler characteristics. The later proofs require a Noetherian base for coherence and finite generation; the Euler characteristic is then specialized to a field. The hyperplane argument needs a section that is a non-zero-divisor on the sheaf.

title: 1971 calendar-year heading
summary: The catalog inserts a calendar-year heading before the first February 1971 entries. It is an organizational marker, with no independent mathematical statement. The next surviving dated block on P000329 reads 8/II--71; it remains in the 1970--71 academic-year chapter.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Bott’s integrability obstruction and analytic continuation programs
summary: The dated Gelfand passage reports Bott\'s obstruction to deforming a distribution to a foliation, explains the easier submersion case, and lists proposed Sinai, Gabrielov, and Bernstein subjects. The quartic-oscillator note at the top of P000330 precedes Fedosov\'s clear heading; its speaker name is cancelled and uncertain, so it is retained here as an unattributed adjacent remark rather than assigned to Kazhdan from the catalog alone.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Catalogued Kazhdan entry without a securely attributable surviving block
summary: The catalog names Kazhdan on 8 February, but these pages do not preserve an independent, securely readable Kazhdan lecture block. P000330 begins with a cancelled name above the quartic oscillator; P000331 has a different cancelled Ka\ldots dan-like name inside the continuation of Fedosov\'s Bott discussion. Neither cancellation licenses assigning a new mathematical theorem to this catalog record. The entry is retained with its attribution uncertainty and no invented mathematical items.

speaker: B. V. Fedosov
title: Bott’s residue formula for holomorphic vector fields
summary: The Fedosov block starts at the clearly marked name below the oscillator on P000330. It gives the zero linearization and the residue expression for Chern numbers, then continues at the top of P000331 with its infinitesimal-Lefschetz interpretation and a real-analogue remark. It ends at the separator before the next-week announcement and the 15 February heading. The manuscript\'s tentative 1965/66 date is corrected by the explicit 1967 bibliography in record 210.
